text.p: PacifiCare Health Systems Inc on Thursday said that was disappointed by its second quarter results, and will fix the causes of the earnings problems in future quarters.
"This quarter's results are unacceptable to us and we know they are disappointing to our shareholders," said Alan Hoops, PacifiCare president and chief executive officer.
Earlier, the company said earnings for the second quarter were $0.39 per share, compared to earnings including certain pretax charges for the same period a year earlier of $0.27 per share.
Excluding pretax charges, earnings for the prior year period was $1.15 per share.
Total operating revenue for the second quarter rose to $2.4 billion compared to $1.2 billion last year.

"We are increasingly confident that the issues that have caused the disappointing results have been identified, he said. "We have already begun the work necessary to correct these problems and expect to demonstrate continuous progress over the next several quarters."
The operating results include effects of the acquisition of FHP International completed earlier this year.

The commercial medical loss ratio increased to 87.4 percent from 82.6 percent primarily as a result of FHP's higher-cost provider contracts combined with higher provider capitation expense and prescription drugs.

The commercial medical loss ratio for the quarter ended June 30, 1997 was also affected by higher than expected health care costs which reduced the current quarter's earnings by $0.15 per share, the company said.
